sentences.text: JUDGEMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.
SCCH-23 2.

The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that, on 02.12.2014 at about 5:40 p.m, the deceased was proceeding as pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HZ-4535 and same was driven by one Nandhish on M.S.Palya Main Road, M.S.Palya, Bengaluru, the said rider drove the motor cycle in rashly and negligently then dashed against the road side electrical pole and footpath.
Due to tremendous impact, the pillion rider by name Prabhu @ Ashok @ Prabanna fell down and sustained grievous head injury.
Immediately he was shifted to Nimhans Hospital and further he was shifted to Victoria Hospital.
He was treated as an inpatient, but the injured succumbed to injury in Victoria Hospital on 07.12.2014 at about 1:15 a.m.
The petitioners alleging that the deceased was 28 years old and doing driver work and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.

It is specifically urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent act of the rider of the motor cycle by name SCCH-23 Nandish and the said motor cycle was insured with 2 nd respondent.
As such the respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the vehicle as such both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
3. Prior to remand, notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement contending that the petition is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HZ-4535.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.

This respondent seriously contended that the deceased himself was riding the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner and by consuming alcohol he lost control over the vehicle and himself went and dashed against the road side SCCH-23 electrical pole and footpath.

Hence the accident occurred due to himself and hence Shruthi vs Shivaswamy on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143143168/
2 the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner.

sentences.text: Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.

Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that the death of Prabhu @ Ashok @ Prabanna in the accident was due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-HZ-4535 that took place M.S.Palya Main Road,
M.S.Palya, Bangalore, on 02.12.2014 at about 5:40 p.m.?
SCCH-23 2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so how much from whom?
3. What order or award?

Aggrieved by it, the petitioners herein preferred an appeal before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.7119/2017 SCCH-23 (M.V-D), wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka allowed the appeal by setting aside the impugned judgment of this tribunal and restored the file of tribunal to the stage of evidence and directed the petitioners to secure the relevant witnesses from K.C. General Hospital as well as NIMHANS Hospital, to ascertain whether deceased was treated at K.C. General Hospital, Bengaluru on 02.12.2014 at 6.30 p.m, or he was directly taken to NIMHANS and to decide the case afresh in accordance with law without being influenced by any of the observations made in the appeal order.

Further more the petitioners also examined the MRT of NIMHANS Hospital as PW.4 and through him got marked Shruthi vs Shivaswamy on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143143168/

11. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly In the Affirmative Issue No.3:

As per final order, For the following:
REASONS 12.
Before discussing on above issues it is necessary to discuss whether the deceased was taken to K.C. General Hospital at 12.50 p.m or not or he was directly taken to NIMHANS ?
13. After remand in this regard the petitioners have not called for the any employees of K.C. General Hospital.
But she called for the Medical Record Technician at Victoria Hospital and examined him as PW.3 and got marked Ex.P.21 to 23 through him.
Ex.,P.21 is the Authorization letter which discloses SCCH-23 that Resident Medical Officer, Victoria Hospital Bengaluru authorized the PW.3 by name Nagaraju to produce the documents to this court.
On the basis of said authorization the PW.3 produced Ex.P.22 and Ex.P.23.
Ex.P.22 is the certified copy of MLC Register.
This court after verifying with original, returned the original and marked the certified copy as Ex.P.22.
Ex.P.22 discloses that "Prabhu s/o Ramesh, H/o RTA on today (02.12.2014) at 6.30 PM two wheeler pillion rider hit by another two wheeler" treated at NIMHANS and referred to V.H.
they have also mentioned the nature of injuries.

In the cross examination by respondent No.2, the PW.3 stated that he does not know in which hospital the deceased has taken treatment before but he clearly stated that deceased was referred to our hospital by NIMHANS.
Ex.P.23 is the case sheet of deceased.

Ex.P.23 reveals that the deceased was admitted at Victoria Hospital on 03.12.2014 at about 1.25 a.m,
(midnight) and had taken treatment from 03.12.2014 to 07.12.2014 at 1.05 a.m.
He died on 07.12.2014 at Victoria Hospital.
SCCH-23 14
. The petitioners have also called the one more witness as PW.4 i.e., MRT of NIMHANS Hospital and got marked Ex.P.24 & 25.
Ex.P.24 is the Authorization letter and Ex.P.25 is the entire case sheet of the deceased.

Ex.P.25 discloses that deceased was admitted to the NIMHANS on 02.12.2014 at 08:16:08 p.m Tuesday and had taken first aid treatment and after treatment the doctors of NIMHANS referred him to General Hospital for further management and observation.
15.
The learned advocate for petitioners argued that the deceased had not taken any treatment at K.C. General Hospital.

On the other hand the learned advocate for respondent No.2 argued that deceased was taken to K.C. General Hospital after the accident same is mentioned in the Form Shruthi vs Shivaswamy on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143143168/
4 issued by NIMHANS Hospital as per Ex.P.25.

sentences.text: They also produced Ex.R.1 which the MLC issued by the K.C. General Hospital.

16. On perusal of the Ex.P.25 in the Form at the time of admission at Col.No.17 it is mentioned that before reaching this hospital visited K.C. General Hospital & mode of transportation SCCH-23 Private vehicle and MLC.
Ex.R.2 is the letter issued by the Resident Medical Officer, K.C. General Hospital, Bengaluru.

The said letter annexed with attested copy of the MLC of K.C. General Hospital which is marked as Ex.R.2, wherein it is mentioned that "alleged self fall from two wheeler on 02.12.2014 at 6.30 p.m, near M.S. Palya".
But the name of patient mentioned Prabhu and permanent address mentioned as Nandini Layout, Laxmidevi Apartment.
But as per another records the name of deceased was Prabhu @ Prabanna @ Ashok s/o Pattanna Gowda @ Patanna r/o Saibaba Nagar, Andrahalli, Bengaluru.
Therefore, the name and address mentioned in the MLC of K.C. General Hospital and NIMHANS are different and not tallied.

Only on the ground that in the NIMHANS Hospital at the time of admission in the application Col.No.17 it was mentioned as previously visited by K.C. General Hospital does not means the deceased Prabanna @ Prabhu had taken treatment.
17.
The respondents examined the MRT of K.C.General Hospital as RW.2.
The RW.2 produced Ex.R.1 & 2.
Ex.R.1 is the SCCH-23 authorization letter and Ex.R.2 is the copy of the MLC register.
On perusal of Ex.R.2 herein it is mentioned that "alleged self fall from two wheeler on 02.12.2014 at 6.30 p.m, near M.S. Palya".
But the name of patient mentioned Prabhu and permanent address mentioned as Nandini Layout, Laxmidevi Apartment.
The complete name of dedeced not mentioned.
As per the evidence of RW.2 one Dr.Nirmala has written the same.
The respondent No.2 has not made any effort to examine the Dr.Nirmala who is the author of the Ex.R.2.
The RW.2 in his evidence stated that who took the patient is not mentioned in the MLC.
On perusal of the Ex.R.2 at that time the patient was unconsious.
The name of attender is not mentioned in the Ex.R.2.
Needles to note that as per Ex.R.2 it might be the patient was shifted to the K.C. Geneal hospital after accident immediately but no treatment was given in the said hospital.
Thereafter he might be shifted to NIMHANS.
In such circumstances only on the basis of Ex.R.2, it cannot be held that it was self fall from two wheeler.
SCCH-23 18.

On careful perusal of all other documents i.e., MLC and case sheets, on the basis of only Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2, the court cannot considered and come to the conclusion that the deceased first visited to K.C. General Hospital and had taken treatment.

The Ex.P.22, Ex.P.23, Ex.P.25 are clearly reveals that after the accident the deceased was shifted to K.C.General hospital but not treated he referred to NIMHANS hospital directly and during the course of treatment he died in the Hospital.
The contents of Ex.R.2 are not proved.
19. Issue No.1:

The evidence of PW.1 and police documents indicate that on 02.12.2014, an accident had taken place and on 07.12.2014 a complaint was lodged against the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HZ-4535.

Based on the complaint, the Hebbal Traffic police registered the FIR and took- up investigation, during which they got examined the aforementioned motorcycle Shruthi vs Shivaswamy on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143143168/
5 from the IMV Inspector.

Ex.P.4 is the IMV report as per the contents of which the front both shock absorbs, fork, head light scratched, front registration number SCCH-23 board, handle, front wheel brake liver, crash guard, rear wheel brake liver of the motorcycle has sustained damages and after inspection the IMV Inspector has opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the above said vehicle.
20. It is pertinent to note that in the accident except the motorcycle no other vehicle is involved.
Negligence means failure to exercise required degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.
Negligence is not always a question of direct evidence.
It is an inference to be drawn from the proved facts.
When a motor vehicle is being driven with reasonable care, it would ordinarily not meet with an accident.
Therefore the rule of res-ipsa loquitor as rule of evidence may be invoked in motor accident cases with greater frequency than in ordinary civil suits.

The fact that due to rash and negligent and over speed riding of the motorcycle had lost control over the motorcycle and dashed to the road side electrical pole and footpath by its driver indicates negligence on his part.

Hence the police have also filed chargesheet against him for the offences punishable u/s's 279 &
304(A) of IPC.
There SCCH-23 is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is collusive and defective.

21 . During the course of her cross-examination, it was suggested to PW.1 that the Nandisha was not riding the motorcycle and deceased was riding the motorcycle at the time of accident, which was out rightly denied.
Except putting in this suggestion no efforts have been made by the insurance company to justify its defence.
Per contra the very suggestion made in this regard goes to show that the involvement of its insured vehicle in the accident is admitted by the respondent No.2.
Be that as it may, mere suggestions do not prove any fact.

The insurance company has not examined the rider of the motorcycle or the witnesses cited in the charge sheet to establish its contention that as on the date of accident the deceased was riding the insured vehicle.
22. Further the insurance company contended that the deceased was riding the motorcycle by consuming alcohol and himself was responsible for the accident.

No doubt the contents SCCH-23 of ExR.2-MLC extract which read as 'breath smell of alcohol patient is not conscious' indicate that the deceased was under the influence of alcohol at the time of his admission to the hospital.
As already discussed above, even he shifted to K.C. General Hospital he was not treated their and the contents of Ex.R.2 not proved.
The respondents failed to examined the author of Ex.R.2 i.e., Doctor Nirmala.
Therefore
only on that base the court cannot held that the deceased under the influence of alcohol and self negligence accident took place.
Further the PM report marked at Ex.P.6 discloses that cause of death of the deceased is due to head injury sustained.
Apart from this, there is nothing on record to show that there was a nexus between the death and consumption of alcohol by the deceased.

Even otherwise in case of an accident of the kind as in this case, where the rider of the motorcycle drove the same and lost control over it and dashed to the road side electrical pole and footpath due to which the deceased sustained fatal injuries, the contention of the insurance company that the deceased who was under the SCCH-23 influence of alcohol fell down from the vehicle on account of his own negligence and thus sustained injuries seems totally absurd.

sentences.text: Another point to which the court was drawn is with respect to the delay in lodging the complaint.
True it is that, there is 5 days delay in lodging the complaint.

But that has been explained by the complainant (PW.1 herein) in Ex.P1, wherein it is stated by her that as she was looking after her husband who was admitted to the hospital the complaint could not be lodged immediately.
The said version is believable because the responsibility as a wife would have obviously occupied the injured to give more importance to her husband than to rush to the police station.
Under the circumstances when her husband was severely injured the complainant was not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the complaint with the police.

It is the duty of the police after immediately intimated by the concerned hospital or MLC visited to the hospital and they have to recorded the statement of the victim or any persons who SCCH-23 know about the incident.
But in the present case on hand the IO or concerned SHO not did their duty.

In any case as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Omprakash V/s Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and another reported in (2017) 1 SCC 724, delay in intimation of the accident or submission of the documents due to unavoidable circumstances, should not bar settlement of a genuine case.

sentences.text: Consequently I hold that actionable negligence on the part of rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HZ-4535 is proved.

Accordingly issue No.1 is answered in the 'Affirmative'.
24. Issue No.2:
The petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed that she is the wife, petitioners No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased.
The notarized copies of the Election ID card, Aadhaar card and birth certificate which are exhibited at Ex's.P8 to 10 & 11 reflect the aforesaid relationship of the claimants with the deceased.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondent No.2, as is SCCH-23 evident from the tenor of cross-examination of PW.1.

Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.

Hence they are entitled for compensation under the following heads :
25.
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that, deceased was working as driver and earning of Rs.15,000/-p.m.

To prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have produced letter issued by Proprietor of Basaveshwara Travels stated that deceased was working under him as driver since one year and paid a sum of Rs.9,000/- p.m with bata Rs.300/- per day.
But in order to substantiate the said fact the author of the document is not examined.
26. Be that as it may, in the absence of authentic proof of income of the deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income SCCH-23 notionally for calculating the compensation.
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2014.
It is trite law that, when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
27. The next moot question to be considered is as to how the notional income has to be considered in the eye of law.

It is relevant to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV)
dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
Shruthi vs Shivaswamy on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143143168/
7

entities.text: Shruthi vs Shivaswamy on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the SCCH-23 injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 02.12.2014.
Therefore, Rs.8,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.
28. The next aspect to be considered to the age of the deceased.

So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the PAN Card and DL of the deceased as per Ex.P.15 & 16 wherein, the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 06.07.1984 and the accident had taken place on 02.12.2014 and it shows that, at the time of accident the deceased was aged (30 years 4 months 27 days) about 30 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '17'.
29.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company SCCH-23 Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident,
the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company SCCH-23 Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 30 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 30 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.11,900/- p.m.
(Rs.8,500/- + 3,400/- i.e. 40%).
30.
The deceased died living behind 3 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.7,933/- p.m. (Rs.11,900 - Rs.3,967 = Rs.7,933/-).
SCCH-23 31.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.7,933/- p.m. and the multiplier '17' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.16,18,332/- (Rs.7,933/- X 12 X 17).
Considering the above facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.16,18,300/- under the head of loss of dependency.

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
33.

In this case, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC SCCH-23 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards his/her father.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.16,18,300/-
 2. Towards loss of Consortium to the Rs. 48,400/-

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY :
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
36. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HZ-4535 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one Shruthi vs Shivaswamy on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143143168/
9 month from the date of this order.

Hence issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
37. Issue No.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH-23 ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,83,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 60%
 Petitioner No.2 - 20%
 Petitioner No.3 - 20%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said SCCH-23 petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioners No.2 & 3 is ordered to be deposited in their names vide Fixed Deposit till they attain the age of majority,
at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioners.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that, on 02.12.2014 at about 5:40 p.m, the deceased was proceeding as pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HZ-4535 and same was driven by one Nandhish on M.S.Palya Main Road, M.S.Palya, Bengaluru, the said rider drove the motor cycle in rashly and negligently then dashed against the road side electrical pole and footpath.
He was treated as an inpatient, but the injured succumbed to injury in Victoria Hospital on 07.12.2014 at about 1:15 a.m.
The petitioners alleging that the deceased was 28 years old and doing driver work and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
3. Prior to remand, notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HZ-4535.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Negligence means failure to exercise required degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.
Negligence is not always a question of direct evidence.
It is an inference to be drawn from the proved facts.
When a motor vehicle is being driven with reasonable care, it would ordinarily not meet with an accident.
Therefore the rule of res-ipsa loquitor as rule of evidence may be invoked in motor accident cases with greater frequency than in ordinary civil suits.
The fact that due to rash and negligent and over speed riding of the motorcycle had lost control over the motorcycle and dashed to the road side electrical pole and footpath by its driver indicates negligence on his part.
Hence the police have also filed chargesheet against him for the offences punishable u/s's 279 &
304(A) of IPC.
The insurance company has not examined the rider of the motorcycle or the witnesses cited in the charge sheet to establish its contention that as on the date of accident the deceased was riding the insured vehicle.
22. Further the insurance company contended that the deceased was riding the motorcycle by consuming alcohol and himself was responsible for the accident.
No doubt the contents SCCH-23 of ExR.2-MLC extract which read as 'breath smell of alcohol patient is not conscious' indicate that the deceased was under the influence of alcohol at the time of his admission to the hospital.
The respondents failed to examined the author of Ex.R.2 i.e., Doctor Nirmala.
only on that base the court cannot held that the deceased under the influence of alcohol and self negligence accident took place.
Further the PM report marked at Ex.P.6 discloses that cause of death of the deceased is due to head injury sustained.
Apart from this, there is nothing on record to show that there was a nexus between the death and consumption of alcohol by the deceased.
Even otherwise in case of an accident of the kind as in this case, where the rider of the motorcycle drove the same and lost control over it and dashed to the road side electrical pole and footpath due to which the deceased sustained fatal injuries, the contention of the insurance company that the deceased who was under the SCCH-23 influence of alcohol fell down from the vehicle on account of his own negligence and thus sustained injuries seems totally absurd.
Under the circumstances when her husband was severely injured the complainant was not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the complaint with the police.
It is the duty of the police after immediately intimated by the concerned hospital or MLC visited to the hospital and they have to recorded the statement of the victim or any persons who SCCH-23 know about the incident.
But in the present case on hand the IO or concerned SHO not did their duty.
In any case as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Omprakash V/s Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and another reported in (2017) 1 SCC 724, delay in intimation of the accident or submission of the documents due to unavoidable circumstances, should not bar settlement of a genuine case.
Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
It is trite law that, when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
Therefore, Rs.8,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 30 years.
In this case, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC SCCH-23 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.
An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards his/her father.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the above facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.16,18,300/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HZ-4535 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one Shruthi vs Shivaswamy on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143143168/
9 month from the date of this order.
Hence issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
37. Issue No.3:
In view of the discussion made supra, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH-23 ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,83,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 60%
 Petitioner No.2 - 20%
 Petitioner No.3 - 20%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said SCCH-23 petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioners No.2 & 3 is ordered to be deposited in their names vide Fixed Deposit till they attain the age of majority,
at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioners.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
